citation.title: Cluster-Robust Variance Estimation for Dyadic Data

standing_assumptions:
The article is Aronow, Samii and Assenova, ‘Cluster–Robust Variance Estimation for Dyadic Data’, Political Analysis 23:564–577 (2015). Printed page = PDF page + 563 (printed p. 566 is PDF p. 3). Everything quoted below and in the targets was read from the rendered page images (staged/pages/p-NN.png, checked against 200–300 dpi renderings of staged/main.pdf). Primes are transposes. The paper writes $\epsilon_d$ for the population residual and $e_d$ for the fitted (sample) residual; the two are different objects throughout.
(S1) Sampling and dyads, p. 566 (PDF p. 3): “Begin with a large population from which we take a random (i.i.d.) sample of units, with the sample members indexed by $i = 1, ..., N$ and grouped into $D = \binom{N}{2} = N(N-1)/2$ dyads. Pairs of unit indices within each dyad map to dyadic indices, $1, ..., D$, through the index function $d(i,j) = d(j,i)$, with an inverse correspondence $s(d(i,j)) = \{i,j\}$, and we assume no $d(i,i)$ type dyads.”
(S2) Regression and estimand, p. 566: “Consider a linear regression of $Y_{d(i,j)}$ on a $k$-length column vector of regressors $X_{d(i,j)}$ (which includes the constant): $$Y_{d(i,j)} = X'_{d(i,j)}\beta + \epsilon_{d(i,j)},$$ where $\beta$ is the slope that we would obtain if we could fit this model to the entire population, allowing for possible non-linearity in the true relationship between $\mathrm{E}[Y_{d(i,j)}|X_{d(i,j)}]$ and $X_{d(i,j)}$, and $\epsilon_{d(i,j)}$ is the corresponding population residual.$^3$ To lighten notation, for the remainder of the discussion we use $d = d(i,j)$.” Footnote 3, p. 566: “If $\mathrm{E}[Y_{d(i,j)}|X_{d(i,j)}]$ is non-linear in $X_{d(i,j)}$, the population residual will itself vary in $X_{d(i,j)}$, which undermines inference that assumes that $\epsilon_{d(i,j)}$ is independent of $X_{d(i,j)}$. The agnostic regression approach avoids such an assumption.”
(S3) Estimator, p. 566: “Define the sample data as $\mathbf{X} = (X_1 ... X_D)'$ and $Y = (Y_1 ... Y_D)'$. The ordinary least squares (OLS) estimator is $$\hat\beta = (\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{X})^{-1}\mathbf{X}'Y,$$ with residual $e_d = Y_d - X'_d\hat\beta$.”
(S4) Dependence, boundedness and rank, p. 566: “Since the values of $Y_d$ and $X_d$ are determined by the characteristics of the units $i$ and $j$, $\epsilon_d$ and $\epsilon_{d'}$ for dyads containing either unit $i$ or $j$ are allowed to be correlated by construction. However, by random sampling of units, $\mathrm{Cov}(\epsilon_d, \epsilon_{d'}) = 0$ for all dyads that do not share a member. The number of pairwise dependencies between $i$ and $j$ for which $\mathrm{Cov}(\epsilon_d, \epsilon_{d'}) \ne 0$ is $O(N^3)$. Let the support for $X_d$ and $Y_d$ be bounded in a finite interval and assume the usual rank conditions on $\mathbf{X}$ (Chamberlain 1982; White 1984).”
(S5) Neighbouring dyads, p. 566 (repeated on p. 573): “$\mathcal{S}(d) = \{d' \ne d\} \cap \{d' : s(d) \cap s(d') \ne \emptyset\}$, the set of dyads other than $d$ that share a member from $d$.”
(S6) Repeated dyads, p. 567 (PDF p. 4): “Formally, suppose that for each dyad $d$ observations are indexed by $t = 1, ..., T(d)$, where the $T(d)$ values are fixed and finite. Let $(Y_{dt}, X'_{dt})$ represent the data for observation $t$ from dyad $d$, $$Y_d = \begin{pmatrix} Y_{d1} \\ \vdots \\ Y_{dT(d)} \end{pmatrix} \quad\text{and}\quad X_d = \begin{pmatrix} X'_{d1} \\ \vdots \\ X'_{dT(d)} \end{pmatrix},$$ and $Y = (Y'_1 \ldots Y'_d \ldots Y'_D)'$ and $\mathbf{X} = (X'_1 \ldots X'_d \ldots X'_D)'$, that is, the stacked $Y_d$ vectors and $X_d$ matrices, and let $\beta_r$ and $\hat\beta_r$ denote, respectively, the population slope and OLS estimator as defined above but now applied to the repeated dyads data.” In this case $X_d$ is a $T(d) \times k$ matrix and $e_d$, $\epsilon_d$ are $T(d)$-vectors.
(S7) Weighted observations, Appendix D, p. 575 (PDF p. 12): “Assume weighted directed dyad observations with weights finite and fixed; denote the weight for dyad $d$ as $w_d$. Define the sample data as $\mathbf{X} = (X'_1 ... X'_D)'$ and $Y = (Y_1 ... Y_D)'$ and the matrix of weights as $\mathbf{W} = \mathrm{diag}\{w_1, \ldots, w_D\}$. Then, the weighted least squares estimator is $$\hat\beta_w = (\mathbf{X}'WX)^{-1}\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{W}Y.$$” (In the display the $W$ and $X$ inside the inverse are set in italic, not bold; the meaning is $(\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{W}\mathbf{X})^{-1}$.) The paper does not define $\beta_w$.
(S8) Simulation design, p. 569 (PDF p. 6): “We suppose that population values obey the following: $$Y_{d(i,j)t} = \beta_0 + \beta_1|X_i - X_j| + \underbrace{\alpha_i + \alpha_j + \nu_{d(i,j)t}}_{\epsilon_{d(i,j)t}}, \qquad (4)$$ where $Y_{d(i,j)t}$ is the $t$th observed outcome for the dyad that includes units $i$ and $j$, $X_i$, $X_j$, $\alpha_i$, $\alpha_j$, and $u_{d(i,j)t}$ are independent draws from standard normal distributions, and the compound error, $\epsilon_{d(i,j)t} = \alpha_i + \alpha_j + \nu_{d(i,j)t}$, is unobserved. In the cross-sectional case, we only observe one outcome per dyad, so $t = 1$ for all observations (i.e., the $t$ subscript is extraneous for the cross-sectional case). In the repeated observations case, we have two observations per dyad, so $t = 1, 2$ for all dyads. We fix $\beta_0 = 0$ and $\beta_1 = 1$. We use OLS to estimate $\hat\beta_0$ and $\hat\beta_1$.”
(S9) Reading used by the validators (the audit's formalization of S1–S4; not printed as such). Each unit carries a characteristic $U_i$, the $U_i$ are i.i.d., and $(X_{d(i,j)}, Y_{d(i,j)}) = f(U_i, U_j)$ for one symmetric measurable $f$, with $X_d \in \mathbb{R}^k$ and $Y_d \in \mathbb{R}$ bounded. Hence collections of dyads on disjoint sets of units are independent, and all dyads have the same marginal law. $Q = \mathrm{E}[X_dX'_d]$ is nonsingular (the ‘usual rank conditions’), $\beta = Q^{-1}\mathrm{E}[X_dY_d]$ is the population least-squares projection, $\epsilon_d = Y_d - X'_d\beta$, so that $\mathrm{E}[X_d\epsilon_d] = 0$; nothing makes $\mathrm{E}[\epsilon_d|\mathbf{X}] = 0$. The limit is $N \to \infty$. For repeated dyads the reading is $\beta_r = (\sum_d \mathrm{E}[X'_dX_d])^{-1}\sum_d \mathrm{E}[X'_dY_d]$ and $\epsilon_d = Y_d - X_d\beta_r$; for weights, $\beta_w = (\sum_d w_d\mathrm{E}[X_dX'_d])^{-1}\sum_d w_d\mathrm{E}[X_dY_d]$ and $\epsilon_d = Y_d - X'_d\beta_w$.
Scope of the list. Targets are the paper's formal results (Lemma 1, Propositions 1–2, Corollaries 1–2, the logistic estimator of Appendix E) and every confirmed error whose correction changes a mathematical statement, a formula or a proof step: P018-E001, E002, E003, E004, E005, E006, E007, N001, N003, N004, N006, N010. Two findings about the reported evidence rest on exact formal arguments and are targets for that formal content only: P018-E008 (the fitted random-effects benchmark has a covariance family that excludes the covariance of design (4)) and P018-E012 (‘an order of magnitude’ against the ratios of Table 1; the validator's evidence is itself a Lean proof). Not targets: P018-E009 (a mislabelled curve in SI Figure 4), E010 (sample counts), E011 (description of a regressor), E014 and E015 (wording and reference-list misprints), N008 (a cross-reference), which are findings about figures, data, reporting and bibliography with no mathematical statement to correct; P018-E013 and N002 (clarity notes); P018-N005 and N009 (not confirmed); P018-N007, N011, N012, N013 (out of scope). Of the headline claims, P018-H1 (Lemma 1, Proposition 1), H3 (Corollaries 1–2), H4 (Appendix E) and H5 (Proposition 2) are mathematical statements and are covered by P018-T26–T29, T14 and T16; H2 is the interpretive claim of valid inference under misspecification, whose formal content is T2, T4 and T8; H6–H10 are simulation and empirical claims.

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: The displays defining $V_r$ (after Corollary 1) and $V_w$ (after Corollary 2) read literally: exact model in which both printed targets equal $4/D \to 0$ while $N\mathrm{Var}(\hat\beta) = 4$ and $N\hat V \overset{p}{\to} 4$; and the non-conformable ‘bread’ matrices (the validator's construction; not in the paper)
canonical_claim.location: p. 568 (PDF p. 5), display for $V_r$; p. 576 (PDF p. 13), display for $V_w$
canonical_claim.statement:
Model. $N \ge 3$; $U_1,\ldots,U_N$ independent with $\Pr(U_i = \pm1) = \tfrac12$; for each dyad $d = \{i,j\}$: $X_d = 1$, $Y_d = U_i + U_j$, one observation per dyad ($T(d) = 1$) and unit weights ($w_d = 1$), which are special cases of both corollaries. $\beta = 0$, $\epsilon_d = U_i + U_j$, and $\mathrm{E}[\epsilon_d|\mathbf{X}] = 0$ (the design is constant), so conditional and unconditional moments coincide here.
(a) [Actual variance] $\hat\beta = \frac2N\sum_iU_i$ and $N\mathrm{Var}(\hat\beta - \beta) = 4$ for every $N$.
(b) [The printed targets] $\mathrm{Cov}(\epsilon_d,\epsilon_q) = |d\cap q|$ for all dyads $d, q$. The printed middle factor, an expectation with no sum over $d$, equals $2 + 2(N-2) = 2N - 2$; with $k = T = w = 1$ each printed bread equals 1 and $\sum_dT(d) = D$. Hence $$V_r^{\mathrm{print}} = V_w^{\mathrm{print}} = \frac{N(2N-2)}{D^2} = \frac{8}{N(N-1)} = \frac4D \longrightarrow 0,$$ and $N\mathrm{Var}(\hat\beta - \beta) - V^{\mathrm{print}} = 4 - 4/D \to 4 \ne 0$: the first conclusion of each corollary fails with the printed target.
(c) [The printed estimators have the right limit] With $m = N^{-1}\sum_iU_i$, in every sample $$N\hat V_r = N\hat V_w = \frac{4(N-2)(N-3)}{(N-1)^2}(1 - m^2), \qquad \mathrm{E}[N\hat V] = \frac{4(N-2)(N-3)}{N(N-1)},$$ and $N\hat V \overset{p}{\to} 4$; so $N\hat V - V^{\mathrm{print}} \overset{p}{\to} 4 \ne 0$: the second conclusion fails too with the printed target.
(d) [Restoring the sum over dyads] $\Omega = \mathrm{Var}(\sum_d\epsilon_d) = D(2N-2) = N(N-1)^2$ and $(N/D^2)\Omega = 4$.
(e) [Repeated case: the printed bread is not the coefficient Gram matrix] $X_d$ is $T(d)\times k$, so $X_dX'_d$ is $T(d)\times T(d)$ and $X'_dX_d$ is $k\times k$. With two identical records per dyad in the model above, $X_d = (1,1)'$, $\mathrm{E}[X_dX'_d] = \begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$ is singular, while $\mathrm{E}[X'_dX_d] = 2$. With $T$ identical records per dyad, $L = TD$ and $\Omega_r = T^2N(N-1)^2$; using the unnormalized block Gram $\mathrm{E}[X'_dX_d] = T$ with the prefactor $N/L^2$ gives $4/T^2$ (1 at $T = 2$), whereas $H_r = L^{-1}\sum_d\mathrm{E}[X'_dX_d] = 1$ gives 4.
(f) [Weighted case: the printed left bread is a scalar] For $k = 2$, let $Z_i$ be i.i.d. uniform on $[-1,1]$, independent of the $U_i$, $X_{ij} = (1, Z_i + Z_j)'$, $Y_{ij} = U_i + U_j$, $w = 1$. Then $G = \mathrm{E}[X_{ij}X'_{ij}] = \mathrm{diag}(1, \tfrac23)$, $\mathrm{E}[X_{ij}X'_{ik}] = \mathrm{diag}(1,\tfrac13)$, $\mathrm{E}[X'_{ij}X_{ij}] = \tfrac53$, and the score covariance attached to one dyad is $M_d = \mathrm{diag}(2N-2, \tfrac{2N}{3})$. The sandwich with the coefficient Gram on both sides is $$\frac{N}{D^2}G^{-1}(DM_d)G^{-1} = \mathrm{diag}\Big(4, \frac{3N}{N-1}\Big),$$ whereas the printed scalar left bread, even with the sum over dyads restored, gives $\dfrac{N}{D^2}\cdot\dfrac35(DM_d)G^{-1} = \mathrm{diag}\Big(\dfrac{12}{5}, \dfrac{6N}{5(N-1)}\Big)$.
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: As printed, p. 568: $$V_r = \frac{N}{\big[\sum_{d=1}^{D}T(d)\big]^2}\mathrm{E}[X_dX'_d]^{-1}\mathrm{E}\Big(\mathrm{E}[X'_d\mathrm{Cov}[\epsilon_d|\mathbf{X}]X_d] + \sum_{d'\in\mathcal{S}(d)}\mathrm{E}[X'_d\mathrm{Cov}[\epsilon_d,\epsilon_{d'}|\mathbf{X}]X_{d'}]\Big)\mathrm{E}[X_dX'_d]^{-1}.$$ As printed, p. 576: $$V_w = \frac{N}{D^2}\mathrm{E}[w_dX'_dX_d]^{-1}\mathrm{E}\Big(\mathrm{E}\big[X_dX'_dw_d^2\mathrm{Var}[\epsilon_d|\mathbf{X}]\big] + \sum_{d'\in\mathcal{S}(d)}\mathrm{E}\big[X_dX'_{d'}w_dw_{d'}\mathrm{Cov}[\epsilon_d,\epsilon_{d'}|\mathbf{X}]\big]\Big)\mathrm{E}[w_dX_dX'_d]^{-1}.$$ Corollaries and estimators: P018-T28, P018-T29. Repeated and weighted settings: (S6), (S7).
canonical_claim.finite_lemmas: (a), (b), (d), (e), (f) and the two formulas in (c) are exact for each $N$; the limits in (b) and (c) follow from them and Chebyshev's inequality ($\mathrm{Var}(m) = 1/N$).
canonical_claim.note: P018-E004 is rated an error, Minor: misprinted target displays; the estimators, the code and every number are unaffected. The formulas in (b), (c) and (f) were recomputed exactly when this list was fixed. The witness has a correct conditional mean, so it is independent of P018-E001. The model of (a)–(d) is the model of P018-T3.

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: The displays defining $V_r$ (Corollary 1) and $V_w$ (Corollary 2), corrected: sandwich targets with the sum over dyads, conformable normalized Gram matrices and unconditional score variances
canonical_claim.location: p. 568 (PDF p. 5), display for $V_r$; p. 576 (PDF p. 13), display for $V_w$
canonical_claim.statement:
Sol's smallest repair (validated.json, P018-E004), verbatim: “Let L=\sum_d T(d), H_r=L^{-1}\sum_d E[X_d'X_d], \Omega_r=Var(\sum_d X_d'\epsilon_d); replace V_r by (N/L^2)H_r^{-1}\Omega_r H_r^{-1}. Let H_w=D^{-1}\sum_d E[w_d X_dX_d'], \Omega_w=Var(\sum_d w_d X_d\epsilon_d); replace V_w by (N/D^2)H_w^{-1}\Omega_w H_w^{-1}.”
Corrected displays. Repeated dyads (S6), with $X_d$ of dimension $T(d)\times k$, $\epsilon_d = Y_d - X_d\beta_r \in \mathbb{R}^{T(d)}$: $$L = \sum_{d=1}^{D}T(d), \quad H_r = \frac1L\sum_{d=1}^{D}\mathrm{E}[X'_dX_d], \quad \Omega_r = \mathrm{Var}\Big(\sum_{d=1}^{D}X'_d\epsilon_d\Big), \quad V_r = \frac{N}{L^2}H_r^{-1}\Omega_rH_r^{-1}.$$ Weighted dyads (S7), with $X_d\in\mathbb{R}^k$, $\epsilon_d = Y_d - X'_d\beta_w$: $$H_w = \frac1D\sum_{d=1}^{D}\mathrm{E}[w_dX_dX'_d], \quad \Omega_w = \mathrm{Var}\Big(\sum_{d=1}^{D}w_dX_d\epsilon_d\Big), \quad V_w = \frac{N}{D^2}H_w^{-1}\Omega_wH_w^{-1}.$$ Hypotheses: bounded data, $H_r$ (respectively $H_w$) nonsingular, and $\beta_r$, $\beta_w$ as in (S9).
Formal content.
(i) [Exact linearization identities] On samples with $\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{X}$ nonsingular, $\sqrt N(\hat\beta_r - \beta_r) = G_r^{-1}\frac{\sqrt N}{L}S_r$ with $G_r = \mathbf{X}'\mathbf{X}/L = L^{-1}\sum_dX'_dX_d$ and $S_r = \sum_dX'_d\epsilon_d$; and on samples with $\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{W}\mathbf{X}$ nonsingular, $\sqrt N(\hat\beta_w - \beta_w) = G_w^{-1}\frac{\sqrt N}{D}S_w$ with $G_w = \mathbf{X}'\mathbf{W}\mathbf{X}/D$ and $S_w = \sum_dw_dX_d\epsilon_d$. Moreover $\mathrm{E}[S_r] = 0$, $\mathrm{E}[S_w] = 0$, $\mathrm{E}[G_r] = H_r$, $\mathrm{E}[G_w] = H_w$.
(ii) [The targets are exact covariances] $V_r = \mathrm{Var}\big(H_r^{-1}\frac{\sqrt N}{L}S_r\big)$ and $V_w = \mathrm{Var}\big(H_w^{-1}\frac{\sqrt N}{D}S_w\big)$ for every $N$.
(iii) [Sparse form] Under (S9), with $q_d = X'_d\epsilon_d$ or $q_d = w_dX_d\epsilon_d$, $\mathrm{Var}(\sum_dq_d) = \sum_d\big(\mathrm{Var}(q_d) + \sum_{d'\in\mathcal{S}(d)}\mathrm{Cov}(q_d,q_{d'})\big)$, and the covariances are the uncentred moments $\mathrm{E}[q_dq'_{d'}]$ when $\mathrm{E}[q_d] = 0$ for every $d$.
(iv) [Reduction] With $T(d) = 1$ for all $d$, and with $w_d = 1$ for all $d$, both targets are the $V$ of equation (1).
(v) [Equivalent normalization] $V_r = \dfrac{N}{D^2}\tilde H_r^{-1}\Omega_r\tilde H_r^{-1}$ with $\tilde H_r = D^{-1}\sum_d\mathrm{E}[X'_dX_d]$; the prefactor $N/L^2$ must not be combined with an unnormalized block Gram matrix.
(vi) [Check] In the model of P018-T11, $V_r = V_w = 4$; in its $k = 2$ model, $V_w = \mathrm{diag}(4, 3N/(N-1))$.
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: Printed displays: P018-T11. Corollaries and estimators: P018-T28, P018-T29. $\beta_r$, $\beta_w$: (S9). $\mathcal{S}(d)$: (S5). $L$, $H_r$, $H_w$, $\Omega_r$, $\Omega_w$, $S_r$, $S_w$, $G_r$, $G_w$ are the validator's symbols (they agree with the prior correction).
canonical_claim.note: Corrected statement for P018-E004 (error, Minor). Repair cost per the validator: none. Using $\mathrm{Var}$ of the total score, not conditional covariances, also carries the repair of P018-E001 into both targets. The convergence claims of the corollaries with these targets are P018-T10 (hypotheses) and P018-T20 (which conclusion is kept); the validator states that this artifact is not a proof of the general extension theorems.

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: Appendix E, the display for $\hat V_l$ read literally (cross term $X_dX'_dr_dr_{d'}$): exact six-dyad logistic fit in which the printed formula and the score sandwich give different covariance matrices (the validator's construction; not in the paper)
canonical_claim.location: p. 576 (PDF p. 13), Appendix E, display for $\hat V_l$
canonical_claim.statement:
Data. $N = 4$ units, the six dyads in lexicographic order $\{1,2\},\{1,3\},\{1,4\},\{2,3\},\{2,4\},\{3,4\}$, regressors $X_d = (1, x_d)'$ with $x = (0, 2, 5, 5, 1, 1)$ and binary outcomes $Y = (1,1,1,0,0,0)$.
(a) [The fitted logistic parameter is exactly zero] At $\hat\beta = (0,0)'$ every $p_d = \mathrm{expit}(0) = \tfrac12$, $r_d = Y_d - p_d = (\tfrac12,\tfrac12,\tfrac12,-\tfrac12,-\tfrac12,-\tfrac12)$, and the score $\sum_dX_dr_d = (0,0)'$. The design has rank 2, so the logistic log-likelihood is strictly concave and $(0,0)'$ is its unique maximizer.
(b) [Bread] $$\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{M}\mathbf{X} = \tfrac14\sum_dX_dX'_d = \begin{pmatrix}3/2&7/2\\7/2&14\end{pmatrix} =: H, \qquad \det H = \tfrac{35}{4}, \qquad H^{-1} = \begin{pmatrix}8/5&-2/5\\-2/5&6/35\end{pmatrix}.$$
(c) [The two middle factors] Printed: $P = \sum_d\big(X_dX'_dr_d^2 + \sum_{d'\in\mathcal{S}(d)}X_dX'_dr_dr_{d'}\big) = H$ (each $\sum_{d'\in\mathcal{S}(d)}r_{d'} = 0$). Score form: $C = \sum_d\big(X_dX'_dr_d^2 + \sum_{d'\in\mathcal{S}(d)}X_dX'_{d'}r_dr_{d'}\big) = \begin{pmatrix}3/2&7/2\\7/2&27/2\end{pmatrix}$.
(d) [The two covariance matrices differ] $$H^{-1}PH^{-1} = \begin{pmatrix}8/5&-2/5\\-2/5&6/35\end{pmatrix}, \qquad H^{-1}CH^{-1} = \begin{pmatrix}38/25&-64/175\\-64/175&192/1225\end{pmatrix},$$ with difference $\begin{pmatrix}2/25&-6/175\\-6/175&18/1225\end{pmatrix} \ne 0$. Both matrices are positive definite.
(e) [Independent form of $C$] With $s_d = X_dr_d$ and $U_i = \sum_{d:\,i\in s(d)}s_d$: $C = \sum_{i=1}^{4}U_iU'_i - \sum_ds_ds'_d$.
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: As printed, p. 576: “For logistic regression, the estimating equation is $$\psi((\mathbf{X}_d, Y_d); \hat\beta) = \mathbf{X}_d(Y_d - p_d),$$ where $p_d = \mathrm{expit}(\mathbf{X}_d\hat\beta)$, the predicted probability for dyad $d$. The plug-in variance estimator for logistic regression coefficients is given by $$\hat V_l = (\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{M}\mathbf{X})^{-1}\sum_{d=1}^{D}\Big(X_dX'_dr_d^2 + \sum_{d'\in\mathcal{S}(d)}X_dX'_dr_dr_{d'}\Big)(\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{M}\mathbf{X})^{-1},$$ where $$\mathbf{M} = \mathrm{diag}(p_d(1-p_d))_{D\times D} \quad\text{and}\quad r_d = Y_d - p_d.$$” The paper does not define expit; $\mathrm{expit}(t) = 1/(1+e^{-t})$. The linear predictor is read as $X'_d\hat\beta$ (P018-T23). $\mathcal{S}(d)$: (S5); here the disjoint pairs of dyads are $(\{1,2\},\{3,4\})$, $(\{1,3\},\{2,4\})$, $(\{1,4\},\{2,3\})$.
canonical_claim.note: P018-E005 is rated an error, Minor: a one-subscript misprint; the authors' code and Table 1 use the correct product. All matrices were recomputed exactly when this list was fixed. This is a finite algebraic counterexample to the literal display and not a statement about asymptotics.

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: Appendix E, the plug-in variance estimator $\hat V_l$ for logistic regression coefficients, corrected (cross term $X_dX'_{d'}r_dr_{d'}$)
canonical_claim.statement:
Sol's smallest repair (validated.json, P018-E005), verbatim: “Replace only the cross-dyad factor X_d X_d' r_d r_{d'} by X_d X_{d'}' r_d r_{d'}. Equivalently, add a prime to the subscript of the second regressor while retaining its transpose prime.”
Corrected display: $$\hat V_l = (\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{M}\mathbf{X})^{-1}\sum_{d=1}^{D}\Big(X_dX'_dr_d^2 + \sum_{d'\in\mathcal{S}(d)}X_dX'_{d'}r_dr_{d'}\Big)(\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{M}\mathbf{X})^{-1}, \qquad \mathbf{M} = \mathrm{diag}(p_d(1-p_d))_{D\times D}, \quad r_d = Y_d - p_d,$$ with $p_d = \mathrm{expit}(X'_d\hat\beta)$, $X_d\in\mathbb{R}^k$ a column vector, $Y_d \in\{0,1\}$, and $\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{M}\mathbf{X} = \sum_dp_d(1-p_d)X_dX'_d$ nonsingular.
Formal content, for any real $\hat\beta$ (it need not be the maximizer) and any data:
(i) With the logistic score $s_d = X_dr_d$: $s_ds'_{d'} = X_dX'_{d'}r_dr_{d'}$ for all $d, d'$, so the middle factor is $\sum_d\big(s_ds'_d + \sum_{d'\in\mathcal{S}(d)}s_ds'_{d'}\big)$, the same arrangement of terms as equation (3) with $X_de_d$ replaced by $s_d$.
(ii) The middle factor is symmetric and equals $\sum_{i=1}^{N}U_iU'_i - \sum_{d=1}^{D}s_ds'_d$ with $U_i = \sum_{d:\,i\in s(d)}s_d$; hence $\hat V_l$ is symmetric.
(iii) The printed middle factor, with $X_dX'_d$ in the cross term, is $\sum_dX_dX'_dr_d\big(r_d + \sum_{d'\in\mathcal{S}(d)}r_{d'}\big)$, which differs from the corrected one in general (P018-T13).
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: Printed display and definitions: P018-T13. $\mathcal{S}(d)$: (S5). Equation (3): P018-T27. $\mathrm{expit}(t) = 1/(1+e^{-t})$ (not defined in the paper). The transpose in $X'_d\hat\beta$ is the correction of P018-N010 (P018-T23).
